chunks: From him, from al-Qāsim, from ʿAlī, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who spoke intimately with his wife in the month of Ramadan while he was fasting. He said: There is nothing upon him; and if madhy is emitted, then there is nothing upon him. And mubāsharah is not objectionable, and there is no making up of his day, but it is not appropriate for him to expose Ramadan to risk.

key_terms.الْمُبَاشَرَةُ: physical intimacy/contact with one’s wife short of intercourse
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the time in which the fasting ruling is being discussed
key_terms.قَضَاءُ يَوْمِهِ: making up that day of fasting afterward
key_terms.يَتَعَرَّضَ لِرَمَضَانَ: to put the fast of Ramadan at risk or expose it to violation

ai.seo_question: Does intimate speech with one’s wife, or the emission of madhy, invalidate the fast in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a fasting person who speaks intimately with his wife during Ramadan. It states that neither such speech nor the emission of madhy entails liability or qaḍāʾ, while also cautioning that one should not put the sanctity of Ramadan in jeopardy.
